subject: CSJ
body: A colleague is struggling to meet a deadline that affects your team. What is the most effective response?
options: Offer to help and agree priorities with them
Ignore it because it is not your work
Redo their work without telling them
Tell your manager they are underperforming
explanation: Working Together: support colleagues and share the load.

subject: CSJ
body: Two team members disagree about how to do a task. As the team lead, the best first step is to
options: listen to both views and find common ground
tell them to sort it out themselves
explanation: Resolve conflict early and fairly.

subject: CSJ
body: A new starter keeps asking you questions while you are busy. The most effective response is to
options: arrange a set time to go through their questions
explanation: It supports them while protecting your time.

subject: CSJ
body: You realise you will miss an important deadline. What should you do?
options: Tell your manager early and suggest a revised plan
Say nothing and hope it is fine
explanation: Raise risks early and offer solutions.

subject: CSJ
body: You have three urgent tasks and can only finish two today. You should
options: prioritise by impact and agree the plan with your manager
explanation: Prioritise and communicate.

subject: CSJ
body: You must recommend an option but some data is missing. The most effective action is to
options: use the best available evidence and be clear about the gaps
guess and present it as certain
explanation: Make evidence-based decisions and flag uncertainty.

subject: CSJ
body: You spot an error in a report that has already gone to senior leaders. You should
options: wait to see if anyone notices
tell your manager and arrange for a correction to be issued
explanation: Honesty and integrity are Civil Service values.

subject: CSJ
body: A policy you work on will affect a group you hadn't considered. The best response is to
options: assess the impact and involve the right stakeholders
explanation: Understand how your work fits wider priorities.

subject: CSJ
body: You need to explain a complex change to members of the public. You should
options: use plain English and check they have understood
explanation: Tailor your message to your audience.

subject: CSJ
body: A stakeholder strongly disagrees with your proposal. The most effective response is to
options: listen to their concerns and address them with evidence
explanation: Influence by understanding and evidence.

subject: CSJ
body: You notice a process that wastes time. You should
options: keep doing it the old way
suggest an improvement to your manager with the benefits
explanation: Look for ways to improve services.

subject: CSJ
body: A new IT system is introduced and colleagues are resisting it. As a team member, you should
options: keep using the old system in secret
learn it and help others adapt
explanation: Embrace and support change.

subject: CSJ
body: A team member's performance has dropped suddenly. The best first step is to
options: have a private, supportive conversation to understand why
criticise them in a team meeting
explanation: There may be personal reasons; support first.

subject: CSJ
body: A friend asks you to look up their neighbour's details on a government system. You should
options: ask a colleague to do it
do it but not tell anyone
do it if it is quick
refuse, because it is a misuse of official information
explanation: Integrity: use information only for official purposes.

subject: CSJ
body: The four Civil Service core values are
explanation: Set out in the Civil Service Code.

subject: CSJ
body: During an election period, a minister's adviser asks you to help with party campaign material. You should
options: help if it is after hours
decline, because civil servants must stay politically impartial
explanation: Civil servants serve the government of the day impartially.

subject: CSJ
body: A supplier offers you an expensive gift while a contract is being decided. You should
options: accept and share it with the team
decline it and record or report the offer
explanation: Avoid any conflict of interest.

subject: CSJ
body: A member of the public complains about poor service from your team. The most effective response is to
options: pass them to another department without explanation
listen, apologise where appropriate and agree what will happen next
explanation: Put customers at the heart of service.

subject: CSJ
body: You are asked to cut a corner that would breach data protection rules. You should
options: do it but delete the evidence
explain the risk and find a compliant way to meet the need
explanation: Quality includes meeting legal standards.

subject: CSJ
body: You receive critical feedback on your work. The most effective response is to
options: reflect on it and agree specific improvements
explanation: Use feedback to develop.

subject: CSJ
body: A colleague takes credit for your idea in a meeting. The most effective response is to
options: speak to them privately and agree how to credit shared work in future
call them out angrily in the meeting
complain to everyone in the team
explanation: Address it calmly and directly.

subject: CSJ
body: Your team is split across offices and communication is poor. You should
options: only talk to people in your office
suggest a regular check-in and a shared place to track work
wait for the manager to fix it
explanation: Build inclusive ways of working.

subject: CSJ
body: A colleague makes an inappropriate joke about another person's background. You should
options: challenge it calmly and report it if it continues
explanation: Everyone should feel respected at work.

subject: CSJ
body: Your manager is away and an urgent decision is needed within your authority. You should
options: make the decision using the guidance available and record your reasons
pass it to a junior colleague
explanation: Take ownership within your remit.

subject: CSJ
body: A project is behind because a supplier is late. The most effective action is to
options: escalate the risk, agree a recovery plan and update stakeholders
explanation: Manage risks openly.

subject: CSJ
body: You are asked to choose between two options with similar costs. You should
options: compare them against the agreed criteria and record your reasoning
pick the one your manager seems to like
explanation: Decisions should be transparent and evidence-based.

subject: CSJ
body: A senior colleague asks you to approve a payment that skips the usual checks. You should
options: decline and explain the process that must be followed
approve it and tell no one
approve it because they are senior
explanation: Follow controls and protect public money.

subject: CSJ
body: You learn that another team is working on something very similar to your project. You should
options: contact them to share information and avoid duplication
explanation: Join up work across government.

subject: CSJ
body: You must give your team some unwelcome news about a change. The best approach is to
options: explain the reasons honestly and give them a chance to ask questions
send a short email and leave
let them hear it from rumours
explanation: Clear, honest communication builds trust.

subject: CSJ
body: A minister's office needs a briefing by tomorrow but your expert is on leave. You should
options: copy an old briefing without checking
use the best available sources, flag any gaps and offer a follow-up
explanation: Be accurate and open about limitations.

subject: CSJ
body: Customers keep making the same mistake on an online form. You should
options: suggest clearer wording or design and test it with users
explanation: Design services around users.

subject: CSJ
body: A colleague suggests a new idea you think won't work. The most effective response is to
options: discuss it openly and test it if the risk is low
explanation: Encourage innovation.

subject: CSJ
body: Your team is under heavy pressure and morale is low. As a manager you should
options: acknowledge the pressure, reprioritise work and check on wellbeing
ignore it until the project ends
explanation: Leaders support wellbeing.

subject: CSJ
body: A team member regularly arrives late, affecting others. The best first step is to
options: shout at them in front of others
talk to them privately to understand the reason and agree expectations
explanation: Address issues early and fairly.

subject: CSJ
body: You find that a colleague has been sharing confidential information with a journalist. You should
options: report it through the proper channels
explanation: Use the Civil Service Code's routes for raising concerns.

subject: CSJ
body: You are asked to give advice that you know is not supported by the evidence. You should
options: say what the minister wants to hear
explanation: Objectivity: base advice on rigorous analysis.

subject: CSJ
body: A family member is bidding for a contract you are involved in. You should
options: declare the conflict of interest and step back from the decision
share the other bids with them
explanation: Declare interests openly.

subject: CSJ
body: A vulnerable caller is distressed and confused about your service. You should
options: take time to explain clearly and signpost further help
tell them to read the website
explanation: Treat people with fairness and compassion.

subject: CSJ
body: You have been asked to take on a task outside your experience. The most effective approach is to
options: accept, ask for support and find learning resources
explanation: Take opportunities to grow.

subject: CSJ
body: A junior colleague makes a mistake that you could easily fix. The most effective response is to
options: help them understand the error and how to fix it themselves
explanation: Develop others' capability.
